name: Sunset Tower Hotel
positioning: Art Deco tower hotel on the Sunset Strip in West Hollywood, first opened as an apartment building in 1929
best_for: Travelers drawn to old Hollywood history

facts.text: Sunset Tower Hotel sits on the Sunset Strip in West Hollywood.
The hotel's 15-floor Art Deco tower first opened as an apartment building in 1929.
In 2004, New York-based hotelier and restaurateur Jeff Klein bought and transformed what had become a run-down hotel.
Rooms and suites have custom furnishings and floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows.
Some rooms and suites have deep soaking limestone baths and separate living spaces.
A palette of neutrals, rosewood and brass gives the rooms an Old World feel.
Turndown brings warm, fresh-baked chocolate chip cookies.
All accommodations get twice daily housekeeping service, including turndown.
The pool has sweeping views of the city as a backdrop.
The fitness center includes a Pvolve low-impact fitness training platform.
Pets get mini Sunset Tower beds, bowls and treats.
The Tower Bar is housed in Bugsy Siegel's former apartment on the ground floor.

highlights.text: Former residents of the tower include Howard Hughes, John Wayne, Marilyn Monroe, Elizabeth Taylor and Frank Sinatra.
The pool sits on an elevated terrace, with views that stretch to Santa Monica and downtown.
Penthouse Suites have wraparound terraces with sweeping views of the Hollywood Hills and downtown Los Angeles.
Townhouse Suites are split-level apartments with 20-foot-high ceilings.
William S. Hart Park, where dogs can run unleashed, adjoins the hotel.

considerations.text: The hotel charges a nightly amenity fee of $52.43, inclusive of tax.
At the Tower Bar and Restaurant, shorts, baseball caps, sweats, sandals, tank tops, phone calls, computers and photos are not permitted.
The pool has a strict no unaccompanied minors policy.
